clue.text: Wellbeing of little creature in Hertfordshire town

indicators.note: the little creature sits in the middle of the town's name, so 'in' signals one piece inside another

parts.note: Ware is a market town in Hertfordshire, a county just north of London
an elf is a small mythical being

explanation.surface: A naturalist frets about the health of some tiny animal living in a quiet English town.
explanation.definitionFit: Welfare is a person's health, happiness and comfort, a synonym for wellbeing.

clue.text: Obliterate memory of complete disaster

explanation.surface: Someone wants to blot out all recollection of an utter catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out a memory is to erase it entirely; a wipeout is also a total failure or crash, as when a surfer is thrown off a board.

clue.text: One not qualified to play one's version about Queen

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the Queen, so 'about' signals wrapping round
giving one's own version of the words play and one's means rearranging their letters

parts.note: R, from Regina, is the usual abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: An amateur actor is told to perform a royal role their own way.
explanation.definitionFit: A layperson is someone without professional or specialist training in a field.

clue.text: Some hope to share national stadium

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the words share national are taken, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A country hopes its people can all have a part in a new sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed space for sport or spectacle, much like a stadium.

clue.text: Develop theory that former partner might place it otherwise

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or lover

indicators.note: placing the letters of place it otherwise means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone works out a hypothesis about where an ex might have put something down.
explanation.definitionFit: To explicate is to set out and analyse an idea or principle in detail, which is developing a theory.

clue.text: Taking 50% of French wine for Henry at the start? Good!

indicators.note: Henry is put at the start, in front of the wine, so this phrase fixes the order

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
vin is the French word for wine

explanation.surface: A drinker is pleased to hear that half of the French wine is being swapped for a king's share.
explanation.definitionFit: Halving something means cutting it into two equal parts, so taking half of it.

clue.text: Fish eater got the woman working

parts.note: her refers to a woman
on means operating or functioning, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A fishmonger notes that the woman finally has a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The heron is a long-legged wading bird that feeds mainly on fish.

clue.text: Frequently, in not such a big case, shows haughty nature

indicators.note: the smaller word acts as a case holding the other pieces, so it signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: less means smaller, not as big
oft is an old word for often
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller frequently packs into a smaller suitcase, which makes them look superior.
explanation.definitionFit: Loftiness is an arrogant, superior manner, the quality of being haughty.

clue.text: Entry pass to small bay?

parts.note: an in is a way in or means of access, as in 'an in with the boss'
to let is to allow to pass, as in letting someone through

explanation.surface: A rambler asks whether a ticket is needed to reach a little cove.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a narrow arm of the sea reaching into the land, a small bay or creek.

clue.text: For example, coming up with old record, you started to study state the earth

indicators.note: in a down answer, coming up means the letters run bottom to top, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
a log is a written record, as a ship's log

indicators.note: only the start of the word you is taken, its first letter

explanation.surface: A muddled instruction about old records and starting a course on the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Geology is the science dealing with the structure and history of the planet's rocks.

clue.text: Method of tax collection for English person to whom the money goes

definitions.text: person to whom the money goes

parts.note: PAYE, Pay As You Earn, is the UK system of taking income tax straight from wages

explanation.surface: An explanation of how taxes are deducted, written for an Englishman who receives the cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A payee is the party to whom a payment, cheque or bill is made out.

clue.text: Left manufacture of oil in collection of shares

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship

indicators.note: manufacture means making something new out of raw material, here the letters of of oil

explanation.surface: An investor puts money into an oil refining business alongside other holdings.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is the range of investments held by a person or fund.

clue.text: Choice about time for surgery

indicators.note: the word for choice goes about the time, so 'about' signals wrapping round

parts.note: an option is a choice
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A patient is offered a choice of dates for going under the knife.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is a surgical procedure performed on a patient.

clue.text: Batting last but run out in opening passage

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is in

indicators.note: the word last asks for the final letter of but

parts.note: ro is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A cricketer comes in to bat last, but is run out at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a cricket scene: IN is the batting side and RO the scorecard abbreviation for a batter dismissed by being run out.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro, short for introduction, is the opening section of a piece of music or writing.

clue.text: Way setback is trying

indicators.note: back means the pieces way and set are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
set as a verb means put in place

explanation.surface: A hold-up along the road is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one word, 'setback' looks like a hold-up on the road; the indicator 'back' turns both the way and the verb together.
explanation.definitionFit: To test something is to try it out, so one who tests is trying.

clue.text: Elemental derivatives are, we hear, funny shapes

indicators.note: we hear means the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: silly cones are comically shaped objects

explanation.surface: Someone claims that chemical compounds are strangely shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicones are synthetic polymers derived from the element silicon.

clue.text: Painting the French find secretive, quite simply

parts.note: painting is a form of art
les is the French plural for the
sly means furtive or underhand

explanation.surface: Someone finds French art rather cunning, put plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Artlessly means naturally and without guile, in a simple, unaffected way.

clue.text: Little tail left out to tickle

indicators.note: out means the letters of little tail are thrown out of order, once the letter for left is taken from them

explanation.surface: A small dangling tail has been left hanging out to tease someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove an L (left) from LITTLETAIL, then rearrange the remaining nine letters ('out').
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to arouse or excite pleasantly, much as tickling does.

clue.text: Feeling people in information technology had been despatched ahead

indicators.note: the despatched word is placed ahead of the rest, which fixes the order

parts.note: sent means despatched

indicators.note: the people go in the middle of the computing abbreviation, so 'in' signals insertion

parts.note: men is a common crossword word for people

explanation.surface: A tech team member feels that colleagues were sent on ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is an attitude or emotion, a feeling about something.

clue.text: Would nun lament over cancellation of marriage vows?

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so the letters of nun lament are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nun might grieve at a marriage being voided.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulment declares a marriage legally void, as though it never existed.

clue.text: One who decides the time in Barrie's play

indicators.note: the time letter is placed in the rearranged name, so 'in' signals insertion
letting the letters of Barrie play means rearranging them

parts.note: J M Barrie was the Scottish author of Peter Pan; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A judge appears at the moment of decision in a J M Barrie drama.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is a person who settles a dispute or has final authority over a matter.

clue.text: Tabloid is back-to fill the cavity?

indicators.note: back means both pieces, the newspaper and is, are read in the reverse order

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A popular newspaper returns to plug a gap in the news.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is a hollow cavity, especially one in the bones of the skull.

clue.text: Lawmaker involved in treason

indicators.note: involved means mixed up or entangled, so the letters of treason are jumbled

explanation.surface: A politician has been implicated in betraying the state.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, a legislative body that makes laws.

clue.text: ABC is, surprisingly, at the bottom

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters of ABC is end up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: The alphabet's first letters are, oddly, at the foot of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means fundamental, what lies underneath everything else.

clue.text: A decorative type

parts.note: reads like a description of a showy person, but type here is printing type, and the fine stroke added to letters is ornamental

explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small finishing stroke on letters in some typefaces, an ornamental touch.

clue.text: Saving incurs tax distributed into a lion's development

indicators.note: the tax is set into the rearranged letters, so this phrase signals insertion
development means the letters of a lion's grow into a new form

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax

explanation.surface: A big cat's growth costs a fortune in tax, ruining a savings plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' looks like thrift, but it means rescue; 'development' rearranges the big cat's letters and 'distributed into' sets the tax inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvation is rescue or deliverance from harm, the act of saving.

clue.text: Team not happy about the question

indicators.note: the unhappy word goes about the question, so 'about' signals wrapping round

parts.note: sad means unhappy

explanation.surface: A sports side is gloomy over the issue being raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A squad is a group of players or workers, a team.

clue.text: Where an old Greek can enjoy the high life?

definitions.text: Where an old Greek can enjoy the high life?

parts.words: Where an old Greek can enjoy the high life?
parts.note: an Athenian of old was from the region of ..., and the high life here is living at the top of the house, in the room under the roof

explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the room just below the roof, and Attic also describes ancient Athens and its people.

clue.text: It has a venomous bite, thanks to natural development

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

indicators.note: development means the letters of natural are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Natural selection lets a creature keep its poisonous bite.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarantula is a large hairy spider whose bite carries venom.

clue.text: Negotiate a special event

explanation.surface: Two parties bargain over arranging a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat with someone is to bargain or discuss terms; a treat is also an outing or occasion that gives special pleasure.

clue.text: Arbiter was accustomed to be turned down

parts.note: a ref, or referee, is an arbiter in sport
used, as in 'used to', means was accustomed

explanation.surface: A referee grew used to being overruled.
explanation.definitionFit: Refused means declined or rejected, which is being turned down.

clue.text: He tickles the fancy of former king with enclosed quote

indicators.note: the quote is enclosed by the other pieces, so it signals placing it inside them

parts.note: ex means former
R, from Rex, is the abbreviation for king
to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: An entertainer delights a deposed monarch by including a famous line.
explanation.definitionFit: An exciter is one who stirs up or stimulates, who arouses interest or pleasure.
